title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that evaluates whether a latency-aware selective-verifier intervention (risk-scoring + fast validator) inside a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while preserving an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), all LLM generations used gpt-5-mini and scoring used a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Artifact-backed results: baseline valid proposals = 399/400; guarded (selective verifier) valid = 400/400. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting is reconciled and archived: model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair call) reflecting the preregistered shared-initial design. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry is absent from the archived confirmatory artifacts; this omission and all artifact references (paths and SHA-256) are disclosed and reconciled. All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and SHA-256 hashed for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration workflows promises reduced human effort and faster, more consistent network changes. Recent proposals pair generative LLMs with verification and repair loops to reduce operator error, but production adoption requires understanding operational trade-offs: safety (unsafe-commit rate) versus latency. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to measure the impact of a latency-aware selective-verifier ("guarded") on safety relative to an LLM-only baseline in a paired design. The preregistration froze hypotheses, estimands, retry and missingness behavior, and the analysis plan before execution. This manuscript reports artifact-grounded outcomes, reconciles execution accounting, documents an exact discordant example for diagnostics, and discusses practical implications and threats to validity.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps research has focused on intent translation, configuration repair, and verifier-augmented workflows. Notable artifact-backed studies include Cornetto (LLM-driven configuration repair benchmark; Protogeros et al.), evaluations of agentic verifier-augmented repair architectures, and integrated agentic validation systems with network digital twins (e.g., Aether). Formal verification and deterministic validators (NetKAT/Header-space families, SMT-based tools, and specialized deterministic validators) are common evaluation backbones. Our study differs: it is a preregistered, paired, artifact-hashed experiment that isolates the verifier/repair intervention under a shared-initial-candidate design and publishes full execution provenance for reproducibility.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (CAND-2026-001) and frozen design: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory N=400 paired intents (same intent presented to both conditions). Model: gpt-5-mini (declared in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic scorer/validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (used as full-checker ground truth). Execution contract set independent_condition_generation=false (shared-initial candidate reused across conditions) to isolate verifier/repair effects; planned model-calls=800 under independent-generation counting but the preregistered shared-initial design yields fewer provider calls—this is documented and reconciled in artifacts (see execution manifest). Sampling plan included 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD intents. Analysis plan: exact McNemar two-sided test for paired binary outcome, paired bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed 1729) for the primary estimate. Missingness and retry policies were preregistered; infrastructure failures would lead to pair exclusion (none occurred). All raw responses, scoring JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs were archived with SHA-256 hashes.
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact-backed): completed pairs = 400; baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 399, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the difference = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Analysis artifacts: condition summary and paired table are archived (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256: 0d6efc16e14d92a1989b0f6d7ed80b8bf8579bff5e364b87aeed4cbd075a3d7e; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8). Execution accounting: planned_model_calls enumerated in the preregistration assumed independent generation; observed model_calls_used = 401 because the preregistered shared-initial design deterministically generated a single candidate per intent reused across conditions (400 shared_initial generations) plus one repair call; provider-call logs and the execution manifest record stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1} and model_calls_used = 401 (see execution/execution_log.jsonl, execution manifest hashes).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On this synthetic corpus baseline correctness was near ceiling; the guarded pipeline produced a single additional valid proposal. The small absolute gain (0.25 percentage points) and the discordance pattern (n10=1, n01=0) yield a null result under the exact McNemar test in this sample. Operationally this implies that selective verification can only meaningfully reduce unsafe commits when baseline LLM correctness leaves room for verifier improvement or in more adversarial/OOD settings. Design implications: (1) shared-initial generation (independent_condition_generation=false) isolates verifier/repair impact given a fixed candidate but reduces model-call variance and reduces calls (observed 401 vs preregistered 800 under independent counting); (2) independent-generation would estimate the joint effect of separate generations plus verification and generally requires a larger model-call budget. Reproducibility: every principal numeric claim is traceable to archived artifacts (examples below). H2 (latency SLO: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) cannot be evaluated from the archived confirmatory artifacts because end-to-end timing telemetry was not captured in the execution bundle; this missing telemetry is logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report this omission transparently rather than fabricating latency numbers.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that compared a latency-aware selective verifier to an LLM-only baseline on a synthetic NetOps intent corpus with deterministic scoring. Artifact-backed primary analysis shows baseline = 399/400 valid and guarded = 400/400 valid; paired difference = 0.0025 (95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075]); exact McNemar p = 1.0. The run is fully archived with provider-call logs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts. The preregistered latency hypothesis could not be assessed due to absent telemetry; follow-up artifact-backed runs should include end-to-end latency telemetry, evaluate independent-generation designs when appropriate, and sweep verifier thresholds on adversarial/OOD distributions to map the verification-budget vs safety Pareto frontier before operational deployment.

limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: deterministic generation limits ecological validity; real operator language and production diversity may yield different verifier gains.
Single LLM: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not generalize across model families without further runs.
Single deterministic validator: safety labels originate from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin semantics); real-device behavior may differ.

Shared-initial design: preregistered reuse of a single candidate per task isolates verifier/repair effects but narrows the estimand to verifier impact conditional on a shared candidate (planned 800-call budget vs observed 401 calls reconciled in artifacts).

Missing timing telemetry: end-to-end latency telemetry required to evaluate the preregistered latency SLO (H2) is absent in the archived confirmatory bundle and thus H2 is unresolved from these artifacts.
